methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Growth → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $1.7B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Atoms is a Growth-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Travis Kalanick that has raised $1.7B to date. The valuation analysis draws from a sector universe comprising 10 peers in Robotics & Manufacturing, including 8 private companies (Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics among them) and 1 public comparable (ticker 277810.KQ).

Given the scarcity of Growth-stage peers with sufficient data density in this sector, peer-median valuation was not applicable—no narrowly filtered subset of same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables met the minimum threshold of three datapoints. Accordingly, the valuation relies on a stage-progression methodology, applying a typical 1.2x step-up multiplier from Growth to the next funding stage. Using the $1.7B total capital raised as a floor proxy, this method implies a $2.0B valuation.

The triangulated range is $1.7B (low) to $2.3B (high), with $2.0B as the median point. This single-method result carries material uncertainty given the limited applicability of peer comps in a nascent, heterogeneous sector. Key variables affecting the true valuation include capital efficiency relative to the broader peer set, revenue scale and growth trajectory relative to private peers, and the specific stage/terms of the most recent funding round—none of which are reflected in the current analysis.
